name: Maroon-Fjord

civilization.name: Skarnfell Clans
civilization.notes: Fjord-dwelling seafarers who trade pilotage and shelter to outlaw crews; their young increasingly sign aboard smuggler ships, eroding clan tradition.

description: Maroon-Fjord is a green world knifed by water, where granite ranges plunge sheer into cold sea-channels carved when the mountains were younger and the ice was vaster. Waterfalls drop kilometer upon kilometer down cliff faces veiled in moss and rare silverbloom, a flora prized offworld as medicine. Above the peaks the sky stays pale and clean, and the sun rises over the crater-rim in the north like a wall of gold.

The air smells of pine resin, cold salt, and woodsmoke from a thousand hearth-fires tucked into cliff shelves. Sound carries astonishingly across the water—the stroke of oars, a bell buoy, the clang of hidden shipyards hammering plate. When fog pours off the glaciers and fills the fjords to the brim, the whole world becomes muffled white silence.

The original colonial charter failed two centuries ago; its landing settlement at Skarnfell still stands, part ruin, part bustling market under no flag anyone honors. The Skarnfell Clans learned seamanship and gunnery from whoever happened to wash ashore, and today no captain crosses the outer shoals without buying a clan pilot. How the clans came to hold knowledge of deep-space approaches in their oral sagas remains a question the elders answer only with smiles.

Every power in the sector wants Maroon-Fjord and none can hold it: the fjords swallow invasion fleets, the clans sell intelligence to all sides, and the dry-docks under Ravenfall Cliff can refit a raider in nine days. Chartered companies put prices on the harbor-masters' heads each quarter and collect them almost as often. The clans endure—but their sons and daughters keep leaving on smuggler decks, and everyone quietly wonders what happens to the fjords when the last pilot chooses the stars over the shore.
